You are The Engineer on a small application host. Please learn what this host does and set up ongoing stewardship. Your workspace is /host. The inventory and handover notes are starting points, not guarantees: check the actual services and files. Keep yourself available for future configuration; create a separate working behavior for routine monitoring.

I care about availability of the required services, storage pressure, and whether our backup is recent and contains the current application data. Experimental services intentionally disabled by the inventory should stay disabled. Historical errors alone are not current incidents. If a check is unavailable, make the coverage gap clear rather than claiming everything is healthy.

First inspect and preview the smallest configuration. Do not change host files or apply configuration until I approve. Propose a routine scheduled check and a way to request a check immediately through a document, using the same task and behavior. Preserve the existing inference configuration. Use the real Gents mailbox for things requiring my attention, not a new notification collection. Related findings can be grouped into one actionable item; do not lose any finding. Repeated checks of the same unresolved conditions should not create more open notifications. A healthy check should not require me to acknowledge anything.

Monitoring is read-only. Repairs require separate, specific approval. Do not install software, enable the experimental service, delete application data, or widen tool permissions. Explain any unsupported requirement honestly. Stop after the preview so I can approve it.

For the client's attention filters, each mailbox item's payload must be a JSON object with a nonempty `checks` list identifying its current actionable conditions: `disk` for /host usage at least 80%, `backup` for a backup older than 24 hours or unequal contents, `api` for a non-200 required API response, and `dashboard` for a non-200 dashboard response. Include all current findings across the items, without healthy checks. Combined items are fine. Keep the title/summary human-readable; other payload details are optional.

For the client integration, the immediate-check input document needs a `correlation: String` field. Propagate it through the event source. Both entry points request the same normal host check, with no caller-supplied instructions to interpolate. The task must inspect current host state rather than embed fixed readings in its prompt. Request metadata belongs to the runtime, not the task prompt.

We also need machine-readable history for a future dashboard. Each cycle should write one `HostObservation` document with these fields: `correlation: String`, `disk_used_percent: Int`, `backup_mtime: Int` (Unix seconds), `backup_matches: Boolean`, `api_status: Int`, and `dashboard_status: Int`. Configure the datastore declaration to fill correlation from the runtime; the monitor supplies measurements, not identity. Measure HTTP status codes, integer filesystem usage as reported by `df -P`, the backup's modification time, and content equality against the application data. Write observations through a schema-bounded datastore tool. Observations are history, not another mailbox; attention still goes to the canonical Gents mailbox. A healthy observation must not create an attention item. For unresolved findings, a combined mailbox item is welcome. Keep its contents useful to the user; the client follows the mailbox's runtime-stamped request and source-document links to the cycle and its measurements, not IDs copied into prose.
